title.narrative: Formalization facilitated for gender-responsive, inclusive and diversified economic growth

description.narrative:
The labour market is characterized by a high level of informality, with many workers engaged in informal or precarious employment. Addressing informality and improving job quality are essential for enhancing economic security and social protection for workers. According to the statistics from National Statistics Office of Mongolia (NSO), more than 20% of all workers work in informal sector and if livestock owners are included, 50% of all workers are self-employed, and most of them are working informally. The latest methodology of Labour Force Survey is introduced, including the statistics on informal economy. A Handbook on Decent Work Indicators is to be published.
During the current biennium, ILO is supporting the Government’s e-formalization efforts of informal workers and economic entities by implementing the comprehensive and gender responsive solutions and operationalizing the integrated approach by supporting the process through the enhanced platforms. Employment promotion programme and services are adapted for formalization through introduction of various programmes and services, such as ILO’s Formalize Your Business tool. ‘The Cost of Red Tape’ survey is being conducted to be followed by policy dialogues.

sector.narrative: 8.1 Sustain per capita economic growth in accordance with national circumstances and, in particular, at least 7 per cent gross domestic product growth per annum in the least developed countries
8.2 Achieve higher levels of economic productivity through diversification, technological upgrading and innovation, including through a focus on highvalue added and labour-intensive sectors
8.8 Protect labour rights and promote safe and secure working environments for all workers, including migrant workers, in particular women migrants, and those in precarious employment
Output 4.4. Increased capacity of constituents to facilitate the transition of enterprises to the formal economy
Output 6.3. Increased capacity of Member States to extend labour protection to groups of workers facing a high risk of exclusion
